LEGAL SERVICE 07 NOV 2012 DILG Legal Opinion No. 62 s. 2012 MAYOR DANTE D. MANGANAAN Municipality of Senator Ninoy Aquino Province of Sultan Kudarat REQUEST FOR ASSISTANCE AND INTERVENTION WITH THE BANGKO SENTRAL NG PILIPINAS (BSP) Dear Mayor Manganaan: This has reference to your 23 October 2012 requesting the Department's assistance and intervention with the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP). Based on your letter and the attached documents thereto, the Municipality of Senator Ninoy Aquino, Sultan Kudarat (the "Municipality"), pursuant to Section 297 of the Local Government Code (the "Code"), applied for a loan with the Land Bank of the Philippines Lending Center (LBPLC), Koronadal City in the amount of for the acquisition of brand new heavy equipment (1 motor grader, 1 wheel loader, 1 road roller and 2 six (6) wheeler dump trucks) for the construction and development of farm to market roads, which is a certified local infrastructure and socio-economic development priority project, using the internal revenue allotment of the Municipality as loan collateral/security. As part of the requirements imposed the BSP, the Municipality is required to submit a monetary board opinion from the BSP. A pre-release condition for the same is a document showing the provincial government's validation of the ordinance. You relate that the above loan is authorized by Municipal Ordinance No. 04, S. 2012 that was submitted for review in the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of the Province of Sultan Kudarat on 20 September 2012. Allegedly the Municipality has not received any advice on the action taken by the higher sanggunian in relation to the said ordinance prompting your Office to seek the Department's assistance considering that the Code provides that an ordinance is presumed valid if no action has been taken by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan within thirty (30) days after its submission. The matter to be determined herein is whether the Department has the authority or jurisdiction on the issue, i.e., issuance of a document validating the legality or consistency with law of the abovementioned ordinance. We answer in the negative. The review of municipal ordinances is explicitly lodged sangguniang panlalawigan pursuant to Section 56 (a) thereof, Article 110 (a) of its IRR, viz. : by the Code with the which is duplicated under "SECTION 56. Review of Component City and Municipal Ordinances or Resolutions by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. Within three (3) days after approval, the secretary to the sangguniang panlungsod or sangguniang bayan shall forward to the sangguniang panlalawigan for review, copies of approved ordinances and resolutions approving the local development plans and public investment programs formulated by the local development councils." It should be noted that the Department is bereft of the authority to pass into the validity or consistency with law of ordinances regardless of the involved local enacting authority. Notwithstanding the foregoing, we are in accord with your view that an ordinance is presumed valid if no action has been taken by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan within thirty (30) days after its submission. This is consistent with Section 56 (d) of the Code, viz. : "(d) If no action has been taken by the sangguniang panlalawigan within thirty (30) days after submission of such ordinance or resolution, the same shall be presumed consistent with law and therefore valid. Hence, assuming that indeed the ordinance enacted by the Municipality has not been acted upon by the Sangguniang Panlalawigan of Sultan Kudarat, the above provision of the Code shall apply. Anent the request for assistance and intervention with the BSP, we regret to inform you that considering the Department's lack of authority or jurisdiction on the determination of validity of local ordinances, our intervention will be of little or no use to your Municipality. Hence, it is our view that if your Municipality cannot secure a certification from the sanguniaang pan/alawigan attesting to the validity of the ordinance or a certification stating its inaction thereto within the prescribed period, your Municipality should then clarify with the LBPLC and/or the BSP if you could present an alternative document in lieu of the provincial government's certification. We hope to have enlightened you on the foregoing. Very truly yours, B. DOQUE IV Director III
